Hi Clara —

Following up after our demo: attached is a draft pilot order form (pilot_order_v1.pdf) showing the packaging we discussed (3 dev seats, 1 prod slot, burst credits). A few open items we flagged in the call:

- Discount ramp: how we tier unit pricing across months 1–6 for pilot vs. annual commit
- Unused capacity credits: whether customer can carry forward unused token/slot credits
- Cap/floor protection: customer request for a maximum surcharge cap if usage spikes during production ramp

Can you share your legal or procurement redlines? If easier, attach comments to the PDF or send a short doc with suggested language. We can propose a smoothing mechanic that keeps your per-token deltas within a band while protecting Redwood from very small unpredictable pilots.

Next steps I suggest: Clara -> send redlines by EOD Tue, Redwood -> Ops/Legal (Marissa & Lauren) to respond with counter language by end of week, then a quick 30-min sync if needed.

Ben —

Thanks for the doc. I attached our redlines (stellaris_redlines.docx) — main asks summarized here:

1) Smoothing & carry-forward: We need the ability to carry forward unused monthly credits for up to two subsequent months (not annual carry-forward).
2) True-up cadence: Quarterly true-ups instead of monthly to avoid administrative overhead.
3) Cap on surcharge: if Redwood applies a surcharge for overage, we want a maximum yearly cap (15% of annual committed spend) and a clawback if forecast was verified in writing.
4) Minimums/exit: For the pilot only, propose a 3-month exit window with pro-rated true-up; any extension to enterprise terms would follow separate SOW.

We redlined a few order-form paragraphs (see doc). Please have legal confirm whether the carry-forward / quarterly true-up combination is workable; our procurement team is sensitive to monthly reconciliations on pilots.

If you can send a proposed counterparty language that addresses 1–3, we can speed signature. Happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow.

Attachment: stellaris_redlines.docx (docx)

Best,

Subject: Re: Packaging & volume credit mechanics for pilot - redlines

Hi Clara — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. Looping Lauren for legal text; Ben for commercial.

Quick, pragmatic proposal from Redwood to bridge your procurement asks and our pricing protections:

- Carry-forward window: allow unused monthly credits to roll forward up to 2 subsequent months (so credits expire after month+2). This preserves pilot flexibility while bounding exposure.
- True-up cadence: agree to quarterly true-ups for billing during the pilot term (quarterly calculations will be pro-rated against monthly usage). Quarterly true-ups can be toggled to monthly at renewal if you move to an annual commit.
- Surcharge cap / clawback: propose a surcharge cap at 20% of annual committed spend for the pilot (higher than your 15% ask to account for short-term burst risk). If Stellaris provides a written forecast at least 30 days in advance and usage exceeds forecast by more than 50%, Redwood will pause surcharge accrual and open a forecast review; any surcharge accrued during a disputed period is eligible for credit if forecast was reasonably relied upon. 
- Exit: agree a 3-month notice with pro-rated true-up for pilot termination.

I've attached a short PDF with suggested redline language for the order form that implements the carry-forward and quarterly true-up logic (redline_suggestion_orderform.pdf). Legal notes: Lauren, if the surcharge cap is acceptable commercially, can you add a clause around measurement methodology and dispute window?

Next steps: Lauren to confirm final legal wording; Ben to update deal in HubSpot and send the updated order form to Clara. If that's acceptable Clara, Ben and I can set a 30-min call to finalize by Friday.

Attachments: redline_suggestion_orderform.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
